question: With router.special.neck_down=bounded-neck (the maze search uses the neck width only in rooms within D of a start or destination pin, D = courtyard plus one pitch; retried after FAILED or INSERT_ERROR like Java's retryConnectionNecked), are fewer connections unrouted than with Java's default room-local neck-down, on at least N-1 of the boards with none worse, with no new clearance violation, no via in a pad, no copper below the board minimum, and a median under-width length per wide net below the shelved Java widening's 40 mm?

java-default.engine: freerouting-rs at the commit that lands Q02.3-Q02.5, after P04's default-tree decision (the Freerouting implementation: room-local neck-down only, automatic_neckdown on, neck_width_um 0)

settings.distance: 2.5 mm of path from the pin (KRT single_ended_routing._neck_pass at 0486e799); the path_mm key is added by Q02.3

boards.passes: canary-pwr: 3 (the Java fork's de7a4fd2c measurement, 88 unrouted, re-measured in the same run by java-default and java-retry-400); other boards: their tools/java-reference/route-bounds.tsv row
boards.board_flags: canary-pwr: --router.min_trace_width_um=150 (the board minimum; D8). Others: none
boards.eligibility: decided from the inputs: some net's class trace width is above the smallest pad width of a pin of that net on a routing layer (Q03's candidate rule, quality::feasibility::candidate_pins), listed per board in the set file

grading: the CLI's result JSON (unrouted, clearance violations) and its widths report (Q02.1: under_mm per wide net); via_in_pad and below_minimum from the A14 parity gate's D8 checks on the SES; canary-pwr also by canary-23's ses_import.py, kicad-cli drc --refill-zones and via_in_pad.py
keep_rule: bounded-neck is kept only if it beats java-default on unrouted on N-1 boards (the canary-pwr variants grouped as one board) and loses on none, and its median under-width length per wide net is below 40 mm (the shelved Java widening's 40-60 mm of 0.4 mm trace). The 2.5 mm arm is kept instead if it meets the same rule and beats bounded-neck on unrouted on more boards than it loses
stop_rule: one measurement run per arm and board; no re-runs to chase a result (canary-pwr moves by about 10 unrouted with small input changes, so its variants are compared together, never repeat runs)

decision_table.pass: keep router.special.neck_down=bounded-neck (off by default); DIVERGENCES line with the numbers; all arms per board in Q02.6's done note
decision_table.fail: remove Q02.3-Q02.5's code (quality::neckdown::{bounded, widen_back}, the fixture and its tests); Q02.1 and Q02.2 stay; numbers in Q02.6's done note and the baseline rows marked rejected

baseline_input: Java's own canary-pwr session (fixtures/canary-pwr/canary-pwr-9511d9a.46bf9e2ef.ses) through freerouting-dev widths: 30 wide nets, 14 with under-width copper, 50.2082 mm under in total (Q02.1's done note)
timing: measured only after P04's default-tree decision (Q00 README, 'Order and critical path'; P00 'Order')
